title: Introduce RAG webhook sandbox + interactive debugger quickstart
author: Nadia Park
description:
Motivation: onboarding teams building RAG-powered agents often need a realistic local environment that exercises tool-calling, external webhooks, and telemetry hooks without needing a production backend. This quickstart provides a lightweight sandbox: a local webhook simulator, a pluggable tool adapter for Node and Python, an interactive debugger UI for stepping through agent decisions, and Redwood Console telemetry wiring examples.

What this PR adds (high level):
- quickstarts/rag-webhook-sandbox/: a self-contained playground with an Express-based webhook simulator (TypeScript) and a small Python tool adapter to demonstrate cross-language tooling.
- debug/ui/: minimal Electron-based interactive debugger that attaches to the local runner, displays decision traces, KV cache snapshots, and allows replaying single-turn interactions.
- devcontainer.json + .github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml to let contributors run the sandbox in Codespaces or CI and validate the smoke tests.
- docs: README with step-by-step runbook, example telemetry dashboards JSON for Redwood Console, and migration notes for existing RAG quickstarts.

Key features and rationale:
- Webhook simulator reproduces common failure modes (slow responses, transient 500s, JSON schema drift) so developers can build robust tool-call error handling and fallback policies.
- Instrumentation hooks export structured events compatible with Redwood Console: prompt tokens, model name, tool call metadata, webhook latency, and sandbox trace IDs. That makes it easy to wire the quickstart into per-route dashboards.
- Interactive debugger focuses on reproducibility: snapshot/restore of KV cache, replay deterministic seed for stochastic models, and step-through of the agent’s tool resolution logic. This is intentionally minimal (no heavy UI) to keep the surface area small while proving the UX.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add TypeScript webhook simulator and example payloads
- [x] Add Python adapter demonstrating tool invocation and error handling
- [x] Add debugger UI and CLI to attach/detach traces
- [x] Add devcontainer configuration and README runbook
- [x] Add CI smoke test workflow that runs an end-to-end scenario

How to run locally (short):
1) cd quickstarts/rag-webhook-sandbox && pnpm install && pnpm run start:simulator
2) In another shell run the local runner: pnpm run start:runner (or python -m quickstart_adapter.app for Python adapter)
3) Open debug/ui (npm install && npm run start) to attach to the running trace id printed by the runner.

Compatibility and upgrade notes:
- No breaking changes to existing quickstarts. The telemetry events are additive; their schema is documented in the README.
- The debugger uses the same agent instrumentation interfaces already present in the SDK; only examples are added.

Testing: CI contains a quickstart-smoke job that boots the simulator and runner and performs three scripted interactions (success, webhook 500->retry, slow response timeout), asserting the runner recovers and emits expected telemetry events.

Related work: Builds on ideas from ENG-2248 (RAG dev feedback loop) and the local replay work in PM-431.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the telemetry schema consistency, the small surface area of the debugger, and the smoke test determinism. For any suggestions to expand the simulator failure modes, prefer adding them as follow-ups to keep this PR reviewable.
